story.sq04.title: Before the Warning Bell
story.sq04.summary: Reconstruct how the reed village evacuated, and learn why an official warning alone did not save it.
story.sq04.s1.objective: Compare the bell ledger with Courier Miao’s account at the old bell.
story.sq04.s1.journal: The ledger credits the third bell. Miao remembers people moving before it. The discrepancy is about timing and shared work, not proof that either witness is lying.
story.sq04.s1.lan: That bell carried as far as the reeds on a clear day. On the White Tide night, rain swallowed half its sound. I wrote “warning heard” because I hoped it had been.
story.sq04.s1.apprentice: Let us separate when it rang from when people began walking. What else survives?
story.sq04.s1.note: Miao’s account, recorded last winter: “My mother had already tied our bedding. Aunt Wen saw water rise backward at the footbridge and sent me door to door. I was twelve. I remember knocking; I do not remember every door. The third bell sounded when we were halfway up. Please write that Wen noticed the water, not that I foresaw a disaster.”
story.sq04.s2.objective: Match the water mark and three bell notches, then choose how to annotate the conflicting record.
story.sq04.s2.journal: The first notch predates the footbridge surge; the third follows it. Wen’s warning could precede the third bell. I can publish the joined timeline or retain each account with a visible cross-reference. Both preserve uncertainty about individual doors.
story.sq04.s2.lan: Do not turn my bad sentence into a new certainty. I did not see those doors. The stone tells us the water rose; the people tell us what they did.
story.sq04.s2.clue: The mark reaches the footbridge notch between bell two and bell three. Miao’s halfway-up recollection fits an earlier departure; it cannot establish a complete household list. Move the three ledger tabs into temporal order before annotating.
story.sq04.s2.choice_a: Publish a joined timeline, naming both the local warning and the bell.
story.sq04.s2.choice_b: Preserve separate accounts with the discrepancy clearly linked.
story.sq04.s2.reply_a: The timeline will say “some households,” not “everyone.” Wen and Miao will not have to carry a legend of perfect foresight.
story.sq04.s2.reply_b: Readers will see both records together. I will not bury the disagreement behind a second shelf.
story.sq04.s3.objective: File the annotated record and inspect the marked footwork sketch at the hub training mat.
story.sq04.s3.journal: Miao’s route sketch uses short steps along the dry edge instead of a straight rush through current. The training pattern teaches Mist Step. Learning it is optional and no story puzzle requires the technique.
story.sq04.s3.lan: The mat is dry. Follow the edge, pause where the mark widens, then step across. We can teach the movement without pretending you have walked through that flood.
story.sq04.s3.apprentice: I will leave the uncertainty on the page. The useful part of the route can still be practiced.
story.sq04.s3.record: Archive addition: residents’ observation and door-to-door warnings began before the third bell reached the slope. The bell supported an evacuation already underway. Household coverage remains unverified. Attached: Miao’s three-step dry-edge sketch, freely copied for practice.
story.sq04.s3.confirm: File the record and make Mist Step available for training.
story.sq04.s3.retry: The three ledger tabs are not yet in order, or the annotation is unsigned. Recheck the footbridge mark; basic movement is enough for this task.
story.sq04.s3.done: Record filed. Mist Step is available at the training mat; you may practice now or later.
story.sq04.epilogue.open: The revised warning record accompanies every new flood drill. Miao’s account reminds the temporary regulator to listen to people below before waiting for a sanctuary bell.
story.sq04.epilogue.seal: When households move toward the alternative channel, Wen’s practical water signs are copied onto their route boards. The retired bell is listed honestly among several warnings.
story.sq04.epilogue.shared: The shared network accepts a resident’s water warning before the next scheduled inspection. The revised record gives that report a place beside the gauge, rather than beneath it.
